title: Bounded-above finite-free model at a cohomological upper bound
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $b$ be an integer and let $C$ be an object of the derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $C$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], equivalently it admits a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded-above complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules, and $H^i(C)=0$ for every $i>b$, then there is a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to C$ from a complex $P^\bullet$ of finitely generated free $R$-modules with $P^i=0$ for every $i>b$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.66.5 (used in Lemma 15.76.2, Tag 0658)

proof.text: By pseudo-coherence, choose a quasi-isomorphism $Q^\bullet\to C$ with $Q^\bullet$ bounded above, say $Q^i=0$ for $i>n_0$, and each $Q^i$ finitely generated projective. Apply the finite-free replacement construction of Tag 064U (proof of (3) $\Rightarrow$ (1)): choose a finite free $P^{n_0}=Q^{n_0}\oplus D^{n_0}$, and, descending in $n\le n_0$, a finite free $P^{n-1}=Q^{n-1}\oplus D^n\oplus D^{n-1}$, where $D^{n-1}$ is a finitely generated projective complement of $Q^{n-1}\oplus D^n$ in a finite free module; the differential $P^{n-1}\to P^n$ agrees with the differential of $Q$ on the $Q$-summands, is the identity $D^n\to D^n$, and is zero on $D^{n-1}$. The projection $P^\bullet\to Q^\bullet$ has kernel a direct sum of contractible two-term complexes $D^n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}D^n$, hence is a homotopy equivalence and a quasi-isomorphism, and $P^i=0$ for $i>n_0$. Composing with $Q^\bullet\to C$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to C$ from a bounded-above complex of finite free modules.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.66.5 (Tag 064U), used in Lemma 15.76.2 (Tag 0658)

proof.text: The quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to C$ identifies cohomology, so the hypothesis $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>b$ gives $H^i(P^\bullet)=0$ for $i>b$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.66.5 (Tag 064U), used in Lemma 15.76.2 (Tag 0658)

proof.text: If $P^i=0$ for all $i>b$ we are done. Otherwise let $n>b$ be the highest degree with $P^n\ne0$ (it exists as $P^\bullet$ is bounded above). Since $H^n(P^\bullet)=0$ and $P^{n+1}=0$, the differential $d^{n-1}:P^{n-1}\to P^n$ is surjective. As $P^n$ is finite projective, the surjection splits, so $P^{n-1}=K\oplus P^n$ and the differential restricts to the identity on the displayed $P^n$ summand. Removing the contractible two-term summand $P^n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}P^n$ gives a quasi-isomorphic complex whose term in degree $n$ is zero; if the complementary module $K$ is only finite projective, apply the finite-free replacement construction of Step 1 (Tag 064U) to the resulting complex, whose top nonzero degree is now at most $n-1$, and add its contractible summands. Repeating for the finitely many degrees $n>b$ yields a finite-free complex $P'^{\bullet}$ with $P'^i=0$ for $i>b$, and $P'^{\bullet}\to P^\bullet\to C$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
